thread:
Emily Tran: FYI I opened a small PR that consolidates a few provisioning artifacts for Dedicated: an autoscale cooldown recommendation, a short migration checklist for teams moving from reserved pools, and a concise SDK example for tenant-labeling. Link: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4502. Please eyeball the wording around SLA and eviction behavior.

Raj Patel: Skimmed. Suggest we avoid 'best-effort' as the primary phrasing. Maybe: 'Dedicated capacity has SLA-backed targets; burst/reserved fallback tiers are not SLA-backed and may be subject to preemption.' Also add a one-liner about scheduled maintenance windows causing preemptions.

Sam Kim: On the YAML snippet, customers often miss tenant labels. Add an explicit example block: `labels:\n  tenant_label: "acme-team"\n  isolation: "tenant"` under allocation.

Claire Jones: Found a stale link to the handbook anchor in the migration checklist. Should point at `#capacity-modes` now. I can push the fix as an extra commit.

Marc Brown: SDK snippet to drop in under "Programmatic provisioning" section: 

```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
cap = client.create_capacity(
    name="acme-team-dedicated",
    region="us-east-1",
    scale_policy={"min_replicas": 2, "max_replicas": 8, "cooldown_seconds": 300, "policy":"throughput"},
    labels={"tenant_label":"acme-team","isolation":"tenant"}
)
print(cap)
```

Marc Brown: Added comment in snippet about runtime preemption for infra events. Worth surfacing in the SLA section.

Liz Yang: Strong +1 on bumping cooldown to 300s. Our sims show 60s leads to oscillation. Recommend adding a short test plan in the doc: 1) spike->scale-up observed, 2) sustained load->stable capacity, 3) cooldown verifies scale-down delay. Also mention verifying fallback to shared model if eviction occurs.

docs-bot: Link check: 1 anchor fixed (thanks @Claire Jones). Lint: docs/lint OK.

Emily Tran: I'll incorporate the SDK snippet, change cooldown default to 300, and take Claire's anchor fix. For SLA wording I'll draft: "Dedicated capacity is covered by SLA-backed latency targets; fallback tiers (burst/shared) are not SLA-backed and may be preempted for maintenance or capacity constraints." Will send to legal for sign-off.

Raj Patel: That phrasing SGTM.

Sam Kim: lgtm

Claire Jones: Pushed the anchor fix as a small commit.

Emily Tran: Thanks—I'll merge after CI green and legal thumbs.

Marc Brown: Quick follow-up: let's add a short note in the migration checklist about verifying tenant isolation labels after cutover (often missed).

Emily Tran: Good call. I'll add that as the last checklist item.
